title: KDP 'No TOC Found' Error? Here's How to Fix It
excerpt: KDP's 'No TOC Found' error stops your upload cold. It means your EPUB's table of contents isn't formatted the way KDP expects. Here's exactly what's wrong and how to fix it.
meta_title: KDP No TOC Found Error — How to Fix It | BookKraft AI
meta_description: Getting 'No TOC Found' or 'Table of Contents not detected' from KDP? This guide explains the exact cause and gives you step-by-step fixes that work.
html:
You upload your EPUB to KDP and get stopped by an error: "No table of contents (TOC) found." Or maybe KDP accepts the file but sends a warning that no TOC was detected. Either way, your book is in limbo.

This error is one of the most common KDP upload problems, and it almost always has the same cause. Here's what's happening and how to fix it without rebuilding your entire file.

Why KDP Requires a Table of Contents

Kindle devices have a dedicated TOC button. When a reader taps it, the Kindle opens your book's navigation structure — chapter by chapter. Without a valid TOC in your EPUB, that button doesn't work, and KDP flags it before publishing.

KDP is also trying to protect the reading experience. A 300-page book with no navigable TOC is frustrating on an e-reader. KDP enforces this requirement to maintain quality across the store.

The Two Types of TOC in an EPUB

This is where most authors get confused. EPUB files actually have two different table of contents structures, and KDP needs at least one of them to be present and correctly formed.

NCX file (EPUB 2.0 format): This is a file called toc.ncx in your EPUB package. It's the older format, used in EPUB 2.0 and supported by all Kindle generations. It lists your chapters as <navPoint> elements with links to each section.

Nav document (EPUB 3.0 format): This is an XHTML file (usually called nav.xhtml or toc.xhtml) that contains a <nav epub:type="toc"> element with an ordered list of chapter links.

KDP supports both formats but requires the one that matches your EPUB version declaration. EPUB 3.0 files should have a nav document. EPUB 2.0 files should have an NCX. Files with neither get the "No TOC Found" error.

The Most Common Cause: Missing or Empty NCX/Nav

The most frequent cause of "No TOC Found" is a conversion tool that created the NCX or nav file but left it empty or broke the links inside it.

To check, unzip your EPUB (rename to .zip, extract). Look for toc.ncx or nav.xhtml. Open the file in a text editor. If it exists but contains no chapter entries — or if the chapter links point to files that don't exist — that's your problem.

How to Fix "No TOC Found" in 3 Steps

Step 1: Validate your current EPUB. Upload your file to the EPUB Validator. The validator will identify whether you're missing an NCX, whether the nav document is empty, or whether the TOC links are broken. This tells you exactly what you're fixing before you start.

Step 2: Generate a proper TOC. If your EPUB is missing a functional table of contents entirely, the fastest fix is to use the TOC Generator. Upload your manuscript, and it creates a proper EPUB-compatible table of contents based on your chapter headings — formatted correctly for both Kindle and EPUB 3.0 standards.

Step 3: Repackage and test. After adding or fixing your TOC, repackage the EPUB (mimetype must be first and uncompressed), upload to the validator again to confirm the TOC is detected, then upload to KDP.

Special Case: TOC Exists But KDP Still Says "No TOC Found"

Sometimes the error appears even when a TOC exists. This usually means one of three things:

  • Wrong manifest entry: The NCX or nav file exists in your EPUB but isn't listed correctly in the OPF manifest. KDP can't find it.
  • Wrong properties attribute: EPUB 3.0 nav documents need properties="nav" in their manifest item tag. Without it, reading systems don't recognize the file as the navigation document.
  • Broken chapter links: The TOC lists chapters but the links point to wrong file paths. Relative paths that don't match your actual file structure.

The validator will catch all three. Fix the specific error it reports, not the general issue.

Preventing This Error on Future Uploads

The simplest prevention is to always generate your TOC from your actual chapter headings, not manually. When you write H1 and H2 headings in your manuscript consistently, a proper EPUB builder will auto-generate a correct TOC from those headings every time.

Avoid copying chapters between EPUB files or editing chapter filenames after generating your TOC — either action breaks the TOC links without updating the nav or NCX automatically.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does KDP require a TOC for short books or novellas?

Yes. KDP requires a navigable TOC for all books regardless of length. Even a 5,000-word short story needs a valid TOC structure — though it can contain just one entry pointing to the start of the content.

Can I have a visual TOC page and a navigation TOC?

Yes, and you should. A visual TOC is a regular HTML page in your EPUB that readers can see — it looks like a chapter list with links. The navigation TOC (NCX or nav document) is the structural version that Kindles use for the TOC button. Both can coexist and they complement each other.

Why does my book preview fine on Kindle Previewer but KDP still shows the error?

Kindle Previewer is more lenient than KDP's upload validator. It may render your book correctly even if the TOC structure isn't fully valid. The upload validator applies stricter rules. Always validate with an EPUB validator before uploading, not just the Kindle Previewer.

What happens if I publish without fixing the TOC error?

KDP may publish the book with a warning rather than a hard block, but the book will be listed without Kindle's "Go To" navigation feature working. This affects reader experience and can lead to reviews mentioning navigation problems.
